I couldn't do this research, so I don't have any notes for you yet. My first attempt to read the sources was rejected with a message saying I had used up my web tool calls for this turn. No pages loaded, so I haven't read anything on Enduring Word, BibleHub, StudyLight, Precept Austin, NET Bible or any other approved site.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. Writing notes from memory would break both rules, so I've left them out entirely.

**What to do next:** ask again in a new message and the tool limit should reset. These are the pages I'll read:

- **Traditional verse-by-verse:** enduringword.com/bible-commentary/proverbs-6/, the BibleHub Proverbs 6 commentary pages (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Benson and others), StudyLight (Gill's Exposition, Wesley's Notes) and Precept Austin's Proverbs 6 page.
- **Protestant differences:** Wesley's Notes for the Methodist view, plus searches of Ligonier, Desiring God, GTY, Spurgeon.org and LCMS for Reformed, Baptist and Lutheran teaching. I'll look mainly at:
  - vv. 1–5: guaranteeing someone's debt
  - vv. 16–19: the seven things God hates
  - vv. 20–23: the law as a lamp
  - vv. 30–35: theft compared with adultery
- **Other views:**
  - netbible.org translator notes, especially v. 26 ("levy of the prostitute") and v. 31 ("sevenfold")
  - bibleodyssey.org on the "strange woman"
  - newadvent.org, catholic.com and oca.org, for example on how vv. 16–19 relate to the seven deadly sins
  - any prosperity or hyper-grace use of vv. 6–11 that these sites discuss

To speed things up, you could also paste the text of any of those pages here. I'll write the notes verse by verse from that, with the URL after each point.
